_strings.@@cb4a614ced8e: Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit for Working Families (EITC) — You must be eligible to claim an EITC on your federal return. If you do not qualify for the federal EITC, you do not qualify for the Michigan EITC. Aimed at low-to-moderate-income working individuals and families; the amount depends on the federal credit (which turns on income, filing status, and number of qualifying children). The 30% rate (raised from 6% by the Lowering MI Costs plan / Public Act 4 of 2023, effective tax year 2023) continues for 2024.
_strings.@@d0ef668b0402: Treaty conformity — MI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: MI starts from federal AGI and has no treaty add-back, so federally treaty-exempt income (already excluded from federal AGI) flows through untaxed -> conforms. Confirmed two ways from michigan.gov sources: (1) The 2024 MI-1040 begins at line 10 "Adjusted Gross Income from your U.S. Form 1040" (the 2024 instructions say to copy AGI "directly from your U.S. Form 1040, 1040NR or 1040SR"), and Michigan modifications are only the enumerated additions on Schedule 1 (line 11) and subtractions (line 13). (2) The 2024 Schedule 1 "Additions to Income" lines 1-8 (totaled on line 9) contain NO addition for income exempt under a federal tax treaty (the additions are: non-Michigan municipal interest/dividends, income taxes deducted federally including flow-through entity tax, MI-1040D/MI-4797 gains adjustments, losses attributable to other states, net loss from the federal column of MI-1040D/MI-4797, oil/gas/nonferrous-minerals expenses (Form 5889), federal NOL deduction, and "Other"). The words "treaty"/"treaties" appear zero times in the entire 2024 MI-1040 instruction book, so there is no Michigan add-back analogous to California's Schedule CA treaty addback.
_strings.@@d69e4211a3cf: Homestead Property Tax Credit (general claimants) — Available to Michigan resident homeowners and renters whose homestead is in Michigan and who were a Michigan resident for at least 6 months of 2024. You must own and occupy the homestead (property taxes levied in 2024), or have paid rent under a rental contract. Cannot claim if total household resources exceed $69,700, or if the homestead's taxable value exceeds $160,700 (excluding unoccupied farmland classified as agricultural). Renters: in most cases 23% of rent paid is considered property tax eligible for the credit (10% for service-fee housing). Separate, more generous computations apply to seniors (age 65+), the blind/disabled, paraplegic/hemiplegic/quadriplegic/deaf claimants, and veterans/surviving spouses (MI-1040CR-2 where applicable).
_strings.@@e1f2986628f7: Home Heating Credit (low-income heating-cost credit) — Helps qualified low-income Michigan homeowners and renters pay part of their home heating costs. Eligibility and credit are determined by the number of exemptions and a corresponding income ceiling using a standard-allowance method (MI-1040CR-7 Table A) or an alternate computation (Table B). Claimed on a separate form, not on the MI-1040 itself. NOTE: the specific 2024 standard-allowance dollar amounts and income ceilings were not independently confirmed from a tax-year-2024 official source in this research (the MI-1040CR-7 booklet was not fetched), so the dollar figures are left blank and flagged unverified.

citation.source: 2024 Michigan MI-1040 Individual Income Tax forms and instructions — instructions: "For tax year 2024, the Michigan income tax rate is 4.25%"; "the personal and stillbirth exemption allowances are $5,600. The special exemption allowance for deaf, blind, hemiplegic, paraplegic, quadriplegic, or totally and permanently disabled is $3,300. The exemption allowance for qualified disabled veterans is $500"; Line 17 "Tax. Multiply the amount on line 16 by 4.25 percent (0.0425)". Second pass: the 2024 MI-1040 form itself prints line 9a "x $5,600", 9b "x $3,300", 9c "x $500", 9d "x $5,600", 9e $1,500, and line 17 "Tax. Multiply line 16 by 4.25% (0.0425)" — both passes agree, and the instructions' worked example ($53,000 - $5,600 = $47,400 x 0.0425 reported as $2,015) confirms half-up whole-dollar rounding.

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: MI-1040 Line 17: "Tax. Multiply line 16 by 4.25% (0.0425)" (Line 16 = taxable income = line 14 income subject to tax minus line 15 exemption allowance; Line 10 starts from federal AGI). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): disabled_veteran ($500 — Line 9c: $500 qualified disabled veteran exemption. NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); special_disabled ($3,300 — Line 9b: $3,300 special exemption — deaf, blind, hemiplegic, paraplegic, quadriplegic, or totally and permanently disabled. NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); stillbirth ($5,600 — Line 9d: $5,600 stillbirth exemption (Certificate of Stillbirth from MDHHS). NOT applied by calc.state_tax.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: The 4.25% rate is the REVERSION to Michigan's standard rate: 2023's 4.05% was a one-year statutory reduction for tax year 2023 only — never carry either year's rate to another year. Claimed as a dependent by another: enter $0 on line 9a and $1,500 on line 9e instead of the $5,600 personal exemption — calc.state_tax does not model this; compute line 9e on the form. Michigan filing statuses are single / married filing jointly / married filing separately ONLY — if you filed your federal return as head of household or qualifying surviving spouse, you must file your Michigan return as single (2024 instructions, Line 7). The flat rate has no per-status schedule, so this mapping never changes the math here. Michigan CITY income taxes (Detroit and other cities; City of Detroit returns are processed by Treasury and may be filed with the Michigan return) are NOT modeled — calc.state_tax computes the state 4.25% line only.
